articles.title: Ms Rachel, the controversial queen of toddler TV: ‘My goal isn’t to be the most liked. It’s to help kids and speak the truth’
articles.summary: Her catchy videos have racked up billions of views, but Rachel Accurso’s statements on everything from Gaza to LGBTQ rights have caused a stir. She talks about screen time, song fatigue and speculation she might enter politics.
body: The YouTube star Ms Rachel, toddler whisperer extraordinaire, spots me before I clock her, and even from a distance and without her trademark pink T-shirt and denim dungarees, she is instantly recognisable by her wave, which is accompanied by an enthusiastic bounce. I half expect her to say, “Hi, friends”, as she does at the start of many of her videos. Instead she bounds over, wearing a classic off-duty mum uniform – Sesame Street sweatshirt, grey leggings, baseball cap that reads “Mama” – and removes her oversized sunglasses. She’s very sorry, she says, rubbing her eyes, that she is so tired – but her manner remains unfailingly, characteristically peppy.

It is only seven years since Rachel Accurso, who used to be a preschool music teacher, uploaded her first video to YouTube, a counting song for preschoolers called Bubble, Bubble Pop!. She and her husband, Aron Accurso, who worked as a music director on Broadway, made the video because their one-year-old son had a speech delay and there seemed to be a dearth of quality videos online that could help toddlers learn to speak.
points: Her catchy videos have racked up billions of views, but Rachel Accurso’s statements on everything from Gaza to LGBTQ rights have caused a stir.

articles.title: Our children may be surprised by what’s in our will – should we tell them now? | Ask Annalisa Barbieri
articles.summary: You don’t have to reveal the contents, but I’ve seen families torn apart by unexpected inheritance plans. My wife and I have three children and seve ral grandchildren. Our will may contain some surprises for them.
body: We gave our children considerable financial help, enabling them to buy their first homes. We have also made sizeable contributions to our grandchildren’s education funds.

Our thinking is that our descendants will need more assistance when they are young: for their education, setting up home, starting a family. And we want to give them the gift of knowing that my wife and I loved them enough to help with these challenges, and that the bequests came from us, not through the generosity of their parents.

My wife’s jewellery goes only to our granddaughters, and the mothers of our grandsons could feel aggrieved that their sons have been passed over. However, we don’t consider the jewellery to have any financial value, as it should never be exchanged for cash.

The financial value of our estate is to be divided one-third to each of the next three generations, with each third divided equally between the members of that generation. We have also stipulated that no generation’s members will receive more than their parent.

articles.title: Water your plants and get an eye mask: 48 life rules every student – and adult – needs to know
articles.summary: If you’re a fresher, this may be the first time you’ve ever lived away from home. So how should you socialise, feed yourself and look after your health? You don’t realise until you leave home just how idiosyncratic every family is, and how many of its customs are tacit, invisible, or maintained by…
body: Anything with blood goes at the bottom of the fridge (although fridge-sharing between vegetarians and meat-eaters should be negotiated first thing).
Refrigeration is a game-changing technology but it doesn’t work if you just leave food near the fridge, even for a couple of hours. Likewise, nothing that’s been defrosted should be frozen again.

Don’t put a cooked chicken on a board that hasn’t been washed since it had a raw chicken on it. Likewise, without getting overanxious about it, exercise caution around all raw meat. Don’t cross-contaminate utensils (that is, use the same knife on raw chicken and then salad, without washing it).
Hopefully, you won’t have a dishwasher, as washing-up is a life skill. But if you do, don’t put anything with an electrical plug in it.

body: This fall, New York museums are mounting an intriguing mix of shows that speak to notions of girlhood, nostalgia, and feminine self-expression across time, cultures, and creative disciplines. As diverse as the subjects of these exhibitions are—spanning schoolgirls and screen sirens—poignant parallels arise, whether it’s the assumed connection between women and domesticity, or the perpetual dismissal of art made by women as craft.

articles.title: An Art Lover's Guide to the Coastal Michigan City of Saugatuck
articles.summary: Lake Michigan's Art Coast has drawn painters, writers, sculptors, and musicians for decades—helping to establish myriad local makers.
body: Lulu Cadieux is a boutique housed in a historic bank with a culinary learning center and thoughtfully curated retail selection.
The shop features items across home, garden, and beauty, and owner Terry Walker plans frequent trips abroad to procure goods (including vintage apparel and accessories).

The region’s largest outdoor draw is Oval Beach, recognized as one of the most beautiful beaches in the country. Pack the umbrella and take in the shoreline activities—visitors and locals alike come here for swimming, sunbathing, and rounds of frisbee. A large parking lot is right next to the beach, helping to ensure a smooth transition from vehicle to vacation mode.

articles.title: Tteokbokki (Spicy Korean Rice Cakes)
articles.summary: Chewy Korean rice cakes get crispy edges before simmering in a spicy, savory-sweet gochujang sauce.
body: Saucy, spicy tteokbokki stars tteok (chewy Korean rice cakes). Stir-frying the rice cakes gives them lightly crisp edges before they simmer in an umami-rich anchovy-kelp dashi spiked with gochujang and gochugaru. A generous amount of onion brings sweetness to balance the chile heat.

Bok choy isn’t traditional, but its crisp-tender texture is a welcome counterpoint to all that chew. Odeng (Korean fish cakes) adds another bouncy texture, though you can leave it out. Hard-boiled eggs round things out and are particularly good dragged through the spicy sauce.

Look for cylindrical Korean rice cakes, sometimes labeled tteok or tteokbokki tteok. This recipe calls for the approximately 2½"-long variety, cut in half on a diagonal. Look for them in the freezer section at Korean and other East Asian grocery stores. Or online at sites like Weee!

This version is quite spicy, with heat from both gochujang and gochugaru. If you’re sensitive to spice, you can omit the gochugaru (Korean chile flakes), as some readers have done successfully. Keep in mind that the heat level of gochujang (fermented chile paste) varies by brand.
points: Chewy Korean rice cakes get crispy edges before simmering in a spicy, savory-sweet gochujang sauce.
